Biinjitiwaabik Zaaging Anishinaabek

Biinjitiwaabik Zaaging Anishinaabek, also found in sources as Rocky Bay, is an Ojibway community connected with southeastern Lake Nipigon. These starting works focus on community participation in food research and a later Lake Nipigon Guardians program.

Read the sources [1] Nokiiwin Tribal Council / Canada North Environmental Services (CanNorth) [2] Anishinabek News

These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

Community participation in food research

A2016 Nokiiwin Tribal Council and CanNorth study includes Biinjitiwaabik Zaaging Anishinaabek among four participating First Nations. Its selected methods pages explain how community questions and local knowledge shaped interviews and sampling choices. The BZA discussion connects fishing, hunting and gathering with Lake Nipigon and surrounding waters. This dated research-design account does not supply current food-safety advice, and its results or underlying private interviews have not been reviewed here.

Read the sources [1] Nokiiwin Tribal Council / Canada North Environmental Services (CanNorth)

02

Guardians and the next generation

In a2023 Anishinabek News report, BZA Guardian Brendon Hardy connects monitoring Lake Nipigon with memories of fishing alongside his grandfather and hopes for his own children. Researcher Tim Hollinger describes community concerns helping to shape questions about fish, water and sediment. These are named participants’ explanations of a particular program. The report does not independently establish current contaminant levels, safe fish consumption or the completion of every proposed outcome.

Read the sources [2] Anishinabek News

Publication: 2016-06

Selected printed pp.1,3,9–10 (PDF pp.10,12,18–19) actually read, plus title/contents for context. June2016 community-based study includes BZA and describes interviews, local sampling choices and community participation. No full report, contaminant results, food-safety guidance, maps or private underlying interviews claimed. Its dated treaty/administrative assertions and old totals are not adopted as current determinations.
